prompt:
Re-design epic manager-agent-flow-event-driven (supersede the 2026-08-25 design with a re-verified one). Read the full brief first: /Users/gavingolden/code/me/flow/.flow-tmp/manager-epic-redesign-brief.md

CLARIFICATION ROUND ANSWERS (owner, 2026-10-25 — binding):
1. Scope: EPIC-FIRST, FLEET LATER. MVP is a singleton manager per epic: launches frontiers with coordination context, detects sibling conflicts, surfaces gated PRs. The old fleet-wide autonomy goal (self-resolving plan-review/clarification pauses across all pipelines/repos) becomes a later/optional feature or is cut — decide per the re-review evidence.
2. Autonomy (owner's verbatim answer): "i want it to have high autonomy and answer/drive high confidence questions for me. Subjective checks like the UI. User-facing behavior can be driven by the agent as long as it has high confidence. If not then the feature pipeline itself should be the place where I answer those questions and the orchestrator monitors it until I drive the feature pipeline. does that make sense?"
   → Interpretation to design against: the manager answers/drives pipeline questions (plan approval, clarifications, interview answers, and even SUBJECTIVE/UI sign-offs on user-facing behavior) when it has HIGH confidence. When not high-confidence, it does NOT relay the question to itself or a side channel — it leaves the question in the feature pipeline's own window for the owner to answer there, and the manager monitors that pipeline until the owner drives it, then resumes orchestrating. NOTE the tension with the brief's hard rule 5 ("never tick a SUBJECTIVE/owner sign-off unless the owner explicitly says so for that PR"): the owner is now granting a standing, confidence-gated delegation. The design must make that delegation explicit and opt-in (per epic / per manager start), define how "high confidence" is decided and calibrated (and what evidence a SUBJECTIVE/UI sign-off requires — e.g. screenshots/UI critique evidence, not vibes), leave an auditable trail of every question the manager answered on the owner's behalf, and keep the remaining hard rules intact (never override a gated verdict produced by validation itself without the delegation rules; never modify shared resources — shared DB rows, usage counters — or prod without owner approval; honor per-model/effort choices). Surface any residual tension in Open Questions rather than silently weakening a rule.
3. Non-epic siblings: IN SCOPE. The manager watches every live pipeline in the epic's repo for cross-pipeline conflicts (file ownership, shared local DB/resets/re-seeds, per-user spend/generation caps, serialized eval spend, judge-hash/calibration-marker invalidation), not only the epic's own features, and tells each pipeline about its siblings.

Additional requirements from the brief (must appear in design.md):
- A short "Re-review of the 2026-08-25 design" section: per old feature (f1–f6), keep / change / cut / already-shipped, each with evidence (file paths, PR numbers, harness primitives) verified against current flow main and the current Claude Code harness.
- Consider at least one radically simpler alternative (e.g. manager = a Workflow script, or a /loop'd plain session + helpers) next to the full event-driven agent; rank options by value, token cost and wall-clock; say why you chose.
- Check overlap/ordering with epic modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture (6/8 merged; f7-workflow-observability-floor ready, f8 blocked) and avoid collisions with the running pipeline add-ui-ux-critique-improve.
- Supersede the old epic explicitly (mechanics your call — e.g. mark the old manifest superseded/delete it in this same design PR); do not leave two live epics for one goal. If you edit/delete the old epic's files under .flow/epics/manager-agent-flow-event-driven/, do it in the worktree below and say so in your summary.
- Field-evidence items 1–7 in the brief (singleton discovery, coordination file, `flow epic launch` seed text, merge-guard override friction, hard rules, durable on-disk state across compaction/restart, terse impact-first status + model/effort honoring) are requirements to verify and address or explicitly cut with rationale.
- The owner asked that this re-design be reviewed at Opus 5.5 / high effort, and for that epic's features a per-model/effort choice of opus/high — record model/effort hints in manifest flowNewHints if the schema supports it.

features.title: `flow epic manage <slug>`: a zero-token sequencer that launches, holds back, and reports
features.description:
Add `flow epic manage <slug>`: a deterministic Bun sequencer for one approved epic that launches ready features, holds back unsafe launches, and shows a terse board, spending zero model tokens. It runs in the foreground of its own tmux window `manage-<slug>` (tmux-only, like every epic surface; refuse under plain shell with the existing named notice) and never touches the epic-design session's `<slug>` window or `~/.flow/state/<slug>.json`. Loop: poll every `~/.flow/state/*.json` belonging to the epic's repo every 2-5 s (epic features and non-epic siblings) and GitHub every 60-120 s with ONE batched query per repo per poll (merged / CI-concluded state for every watched PR and every open PR, so out-of-band merges are seen); on any change run the existing pure `reconcile()` + `classifyEvent()` (`bin/lib/epic-reconcile.ts`, which already floors on the committed status board), compute the frontier (`computeFrontier` in `bin/flow-epic-dag.ts`), and launch up to `epic.maxParallel` through `launchFeature()` / `flow epic launch` (`bin/lib/epic-launch.ts`). Drift guard (the reason PR #420 deleted the 2026-07 watch loop: it trusted `run.json`): before each launch run a mechanical duplicate check — no PR, branch, worktree, or live state file for the feature's id-derived slug or its `--epic <slug>/<id>` tag — and on any ambiguity (an `orphan` row, an unbound PR or branch, a manifest/run.json mismatch) do NOT launch or repair that node; show `drift: run /flow-epic-run reconcile-drift` on the board and keep launching independent branches. Never add judgment, retries, redirects, budgets, or a phase machine. State in `~/.flow/state/managers/<slug>/` (outside `listStates()`): `manager.json` {pid, procStartedAt, heartbeatAt, autonomy, startedAt} written under `withFileLockSync` (`bin/lib/lock.ts`), and one append-only `log.jsonl` (launch, hold, drift-halt, merged-observed, plus later delegated-decision entries). Singleton by state liveness (`bin/lib/liveness.ts`): a second `flow epic manage <slug>` while one is live refuses and prints the window name and how to switch to it. `flow epic status <slug>` and `flow ls` show the live sequencer and its heartbeat age (stale beyond 3 poll intervals). Board: the pause-output contract's impact-first slots, one line per feature that needs the owner (`gated`, `needs-human`, a pending pause) naming the window where they answer, plus one `flow-notify` per new owner-needed event; the epic ends with a final board when `reconcile()` says done. Ctrl-C (async sleep — the #390 loop swallowed SIGINT) and window close stop it with no effect on launched pipelines; a restart rebuilds from disk and GitHub. Manifest: make `flowNewHints.model` a typed `ModelAlias` hint in `bin/lib/epic-manifest-schema.ts`, mapped in `buildFeatureCreateArgs` (CLI `--model` > hint > config); add an optional typed `waitFor` string on Feature — a node with `waitFor` is never launched (`flow epic launch` refuses it with a named error, so `/flow-epic-run` cannot launch it either), shows on the board as `waiting on: <waitFor>`, and completes only via `flow epic bind <epic> <id> --external "<ref>"`. Model/effort flags, mirroring `flow feature create` / `flow epic create` / `flow epic run`: `flow epic manage <slug> [--model <opus|haiku|sonnet|fable>] [--effort <low|medium|high|xhigh|max>]`, validated by the same alias/level parsers those commands use, persisted in `manager.json` {model, effort} (precedence: flag > `config.models.manager` / `config.efforts.manager` > opus/high), shown on the board header, and listed in help and completions. They set (a) the model/effort of every model call made on the manager's behalf — the delegated-judgment `flow-claude-headless` calls later features add read them from `manager.json` — and (b) the fallback for a launched feature that has no manifest `model`/`effort` hint (per-feature precedence: `flow epic launch` CLI override > manifest hint > manager flag > config). The sequencer loop itself still makes zero model calls. `--autonomy observe` is the only autonomy value this feature accepts (the flag exists so a later feature can add `high`). Governance in lockstep: AGENTS.md and `.claude/rules/flow-supervisor-contracts.md` name `flow epic manage` as a sanctioned zero-fan-out, zero-form, never-merges surface; `docs/target-architecture.md`'s 'not a long-running daemon' line names this one owner-started foreground exception; `skills/pipeline/flow-epic-run/SKILL.md` gets one hands-table row pointing at the sequencer (its no-loop invariants stay true of the playbook itself); help, completions; rewrite the stale 'watch loop' comments in `bin/lib/epic-launch.ts`. Tests next door: reconcile-driven launch matrix over fixture state dirs, the three PR #420 drift scenarios (recreated slug, out-of-band merge, manifest drift) plus an unknown-slug pipeline for an epic feature (all must halt, not launch), `waitFor` refusal, singleton refusal, SIGINT exit, heartbeat staleness, gh-failure degradation to a board line, and a repo-scoping test (another repo's state never counts).

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `f1-epic-sequencer`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D1-D3: the deterministic poll/reconcile/launch loop, the drift and duplicate checks that answer why PR #420 deleted the 2026-07 loop, the manager state file and log, the typed model hint, and waitFor nodes.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN the frontier is non-empty and in-flight features are below epic.maxParallel THE SYSTEM SHALL launch the next feature through flow epic launch with the manifest model and effort hints (fixture test asserts the argv)

WHEN a pipeline's state file changes phase THE SYSTEM SHALL redraw the board within 10 seconds, and WHEN a watched PR merges it SHALL observe it within 120 seconds using one batched GitHub query per repo per poll

WHEN any of the three PR #420 drift scenarios (recreated slug, out-of-band merge, manifest drift) or an unknown-slug pipeline for an epic feature is present THE SYSTEM SHALL not launch that feature and SHALL show a reconcile-drift line naming /flow-epic-run
WHEN a feature has a waitFor value THE SYSTEM SHALL never launch it, and flow epic launch SHALL refuse it with a named error
WHEN flow epic manage runs while the epic's manager.json shows a live sequencer THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse and print the live window name, and flow epic status and flow ls SHALL show its heartbeat age
WHEN the sequencer receives SIGINT THE SYSTEM SHALL exit 0 within one second without touching any launched pipeline, and a restart SHALL rebuild the same board from disk
WHEN the sequencer runs idle for an hour THE SYSTEM SHALL make zero model calls (no claude or flow-claude-headless spawn in the test seam)

WHEN flow epic manage runs with --model and --effort THE SYSTEM SHALL validate them like flow epic create, persist them in manager.json, show them on the board, and pass them to a launched feature only when that feature's manifest has no model/effort hint (fixture test asserts both argv cases)

features.title: The executive: an owner charter, an executive review that approves, presses, or defers, and the owner grant that lets it act
features.rationale: Hides D8: how the owner's perspective is written down, how an executive review decides act / challenge / defer, and the grant that lets that decision stand in for the owner's keystroke. Root because it needs no sequencer: /flow-epic-run uses it the day it merges.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN an owner grant is live for an epic and one of its features reaches plan approval THE SYSTEM SHALL run the executive review before pausing and, on an approve decision whose hard preconditions pass, continue without pausing, record the decision with rationale, confidence and door type, print the disclosure line, and stamp the PR body

WHEN the executive review returns challenge THE SYSTEM SHALL run the pipeline's own plan revision pass with the challenge memo as the redirect, re-review, and after at most two challenge rounds decide approve or defer

WHEN the executive review returns defer, or any hard precondition fails, or the decision is a one-way door THE SYSTEM SHALL pause in the pipeline's own window as today with the executive's single recommendation and the one-word replies that accept or reject it
WHEN no grant is live, or the slug is not a feature of the granted epic THE SYSTEM SHALL never run a delegated decision
WHEN the owner corrects a delegated decision THE SYSTEM SHALL let that correction be added as a line in the charter section of the user-level product brief, which every later executive review reads

WHEN /flow-epic-run takes a step and a feature merged since the last step THE SYSTEM SHALL run one executive wave review, apply a reorder of unstarted features, and show any defer / cut / add / goal change only as a proposal for the owner

WHEN the executive review runs THE SYSTEM SHALL use the grant's model and effort (default opus/high) and stay within a per-call budget cap, and SHALL pause rather than decide when the call fails or is skipped
WHEN the executive's confidence is medium or low, or the door is one-way THE SYSTEM SHALL pause in the pipeline's own window exactly as today
features.description:
Give the manager a brain: the owner's perspective written down once, an executive review that applies it at decision points, and an owner grant that lets the review's decision stand in for the owner's keystroke. Owner charter: extend the user-level product brief (`~/.flow/product.md`, seeded by `bin/lib/product-brief-seed.ts`, read by `flow-product-brief`) with a `## Deciding on my behalf` section holding the charter in the epic design's `## Executive charter` (goal-first, question the premise, ruthless prioritization, simplicity unless later change is expensive, two-way vs one-way doors, press don't rubber-stamp, outside view + pre-mortem, accountability, owner rulings win, bias to action); update the seed so new installs get it; never fork a second values file. Executive review: new bare-name helper `flow-exec-review` (`bin/flow-exec-review.ts`, registered in `bin/lib/modules.ts`, pre-approved in `bin/lib/pipeline-allow-rules.ts`) with `review --kind plan|wave --epic <slug> [--slug <feature>]`: assembles a bounded decision packet the feature agent does not have — the epic goal and design, the manifest neighbourhood, the product brief + charter, the charter's standing corrections and prior decisions from the epic log, sibling pipeline phases, the plan or merged PR, and the cross-model review — and makes ONE `flow-claude-headless` call (model/effort from the grant, default opus/high, `--max-budget-usd` capped, read-only tools) returning a schema-validated envelope {decision: approve|challenge|defer (plan) or continue|reorder|propose|escalate (wave), doorType: two-way|one-way, confidence, rationale, challenges[] (max 3, each a question plus the evidence that would change the decision), recommendation}. Hard preconditions it never waives (mechanical, checked before the call): the cross-model plan review ran with a non-Claude reviewer engaged; every `[anchor: …]` resolves; `flow-plan-lint` clean; no proposed production, shared-database, usage-counter, or shared-service action (always one-way, always defer). Grant: `flow epic grant <epic> --autonomy high|off [--model <alias>] [--effort <level>]` (owner-typed CLI; `off` withdraws it) writes `~/.flow/state/managers/<epic>/grant.json` {epic, classes:[plan], grantedAt, grantedBy: owner-cli, model, effort} under `withFileLockSync`; f1's sequencer later reads the same directory. Pipeline: in `skills/pipeline/flow-pipeline/references/phases/step-04-approval.md` (and its SKILL.md pointer), BEFORE rendering `plan-pending-review`, an epic feature with a live grant runs `flow-exec-review review --kind plan`; approve ⇒ append the decision to `~/.flow/state/managers/<epic>/log.jsonl`, print `Approved by the epic executive under your grant (decision <id>)`, stamp the PR body draft, continue past `checkpoint-pending-clear`; challenge ⇒ the existing revision pass with the challenge memo as the redirect, re-review, max two rounds; defer/fail ⇒ the normal pause with the recommendation and one-word replies. Interviews and clarifications are not delegated. Confidence uses flow's existing `[confidence: high|medium|low]` vocabulary: the executive acts only on high confidence AND a two-way door; anything else pauses in the feature window as today. Decision record: no new store — the f1 `log.jsonl` line, the PR-body stamp, and the board digest; an owner correction becomes a line the owner (or the session, on the owner's say-so) adds to the charter section, which every review reads. The charter is always read from the user-level `~/.flow/product.md`, even in a repo whose own `.flow/product.md` shadows the user brief for product review (`bin/flow-product-brief.ts` resolves repo-first). `/flow-epic-run`: add a wave-review step to launch-next (one `flow-exec-review review --kind wave` per newly observed merge; the decision is continue / reorder / propose / escalate: a reorder of unstarted features is a two-way door the playbook applies and logs; deferring or cutting a feature, adding one, or changing the epic goal is never applied — it is a proposal shown to the owner with its rationale, and an owner `yes` routes it through amend-manifest) — the executive reorders on its own and proposes every reshape. Write the review prompt in `references/executive-review.md` (charter text not duplicated — it is read from the product brief) and lint its hard-rule anchors in `bin/skill-md-lint.test.ts` (never merge, never `--record-override`, never answer prod/shared-resource actions, never send-keys, owner rulings win). Tests next door: envelope schema, every hard precondition's fail path, one-way door ⇒ defer, challenge-round cap, grant scope (non-epic or other-epic slug never passes), budget/headless failure ⇒ pause, charter read from the user-level brief even when a repo brief exists, propose never mutates the manifest, and the record/stamp shape. Shared with f1: the `~/.flow/state/managers/<epic>/` directory and `log.jsonl` line format — whichever merges second adopts the first's shape.

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `f5-executive-judgment`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.

features.title: A generated per-repo coordination file every pipeline reads, fed by the sequencer
features.description:
Add sibling coordination for every live pipeline in a repo, epic or not, and wire it into the epic sequencer from `f1-epic-sequencer`. New bare-name helper `flow-coord` (`bin/flow-coord.ts`, registered in `bin/lib/modules.ts`, pre-approved in `bin/lib/pipeline-allow-rules.ts`): `refresh` builds `~/.flow/coordination/<repo-key>.md` + `.json` from every live `~/.flow/state/*.json` in that repo, under `withFileLockSync` so any number of writers (several epic sequencers, standalone pipelines) produce the same content: each pipeline's actual diff against its base (authoritative), its planned paths (informational only), overlaps between actual diffs with the standing yield rule (surgical edits; the second to merge resolves; never force-push), and the rules from the repo's optional committed `.flow/coordination-notes.json` — a list of `{ rule: string, paths?: string[] }` in plain words (one local database never reset, announce re-seeds, a daily generation cap, serialized eval spend, a judge hash tied to a calibration marker); `brief --slug <s>` prints one pipeline's slice (its overlaps, the yield rule, every notes rule whose paths match its files, and the rules with no paths); `log` appends a line to the file's append-only log. Pipelines pull, never get messaged: `/flow-pipeline` publishes the plan's named paths into state (`plannedPaths`) right after planning, and reads `flow-coord refresh && flow-coord brief --slug "$FLOW_SLUG"` at three fixed points — into discovery at step 3, at the start of step 5 implementation (after concurrent plans have settled), and before the step 10 merge guard — degrading to a named skip when the helper is absent. Add `flow epic launch <epic> <id> --context-file <path>`, which appends a delimited 'Coordination context' block before the pointer sentence of the dispatched seed. In the sequencer: run `flow-coord refresh` on every pass; launch every feature with the current brief via `--context-file`; hold back a ready feature whose declared `sharedArtifacts` intersect any live pipeline's actual diff in the repo (log a `hold` entry and a board line naming the blocking pipeline; epic-internal declared overlaps are already serialized by `flow-epic-dag --validate`'s `unordered-producers` check, so this covers other epics and non-epic siblings); show new actual-diff overlaps as board lines. Document `.flow/coordination-notes.json` in `references/consumer-repo-contract.md` next to the optional `.flow/ui-validation.json`. Tests next door: ownership from fixture diffs, overlap + yield rule, notes path matching, lock contention (two concurrent refreshes give one consistent file), brief slicing, `--context-file` placement before the pointer sentence, hold-back on a sibling's overlapping diff, and the helper-absent skip.

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `f2-repo-coordination`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D4: ownership derivation from actual diffs, the yield rule, the free-text notes format, the three pull-based read points, and the launch hold-back.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN two live pipelines in one repo have overlapping files in their actual diffs THE SYSTEM SHALL list the overlap with the yield rule in the coordination file and in both pipelines' briefs
WHEN two flow-coord refresh calls run concurrently THE SYSTEM SHALL produce one consistent file (lock contention test)
WHEN a ready epic feature's declared sharedArtifacts intersect a live sibling's actual diff THE SYSTEM SHALL hold it back with a board line naming the blocking pipeline and a hold log entry
WHEN the sequencer launches a feature THE SYSTEM SHALL pass the current brief through flow epic launch --context-file, placed before the pointer sentence
WHEN a pipeline reaches planning, the start of implementation, or the merge guard THE SYSTEM SHALL read its brief, and WHEN flow-coord is absent it SHALL record a named skip
WHEN the repo commits .flow/coordination-notes.json THE SYSTEM SHALL include every rule whose paths match a pipeline's files, and every rule without paths, in that pipeline's brief

features.title: Wait node: the sequencer has driven one real wave
features.description:
Wait node — do not build anything. This node is satisfied when the epic sequencer from `f1-epic-sequencer` (`flow epic manage`) has driven one real feature from launch to merged on a real epic (this epic's `f2-repo-coordination` or any econ-data epic feature), with no hand `flow feature create`, launch, or bind for that feature and no drift halt left unexplained in `~/.flow/state/managers/<slug>/log.jsonl`. It exists so the sequencer is not given executive autonomy (`f3-sequencer-executive`) until it is proven. The owner records it with `flow epic bind re-design-epic-manager-agent w1-managed-wave --external "<PR of that feature>"`. If a pipeline was launched from this node by mistake, make no code change, stop at triage as no-change, and report that this node must be bound with `flow epic bind ... --external` instead.

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `w1-managed-wave`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D7 (first condition): delegated answers are not built until the sequencer has proven itself on a real wave; enforced by the frontier, not by prose.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN the owner binds this node with flow epic bind --external THE SYSTEM SHALL classify it merged and unblock f3-sequencer-executive
WHEN this node is unbound THE SYSTEM SHALL never launch it (flow epic launch refuses a waitFor node)
features.waitFor: one feature launched by flow epic manage and merged with no hand launch or bind and no unexplained drift halt

features.title: The sequencer runs the executive: wave reviews at every merge, decisions on the board, and a digest of what was decided for the owner
features.description:
Wire f1's zero-token sequencer to f5's executive without putting judgment in the loop. `flow epic manage <slug> --autonomy high` (extends f1's `--autonomy observe`) requires a live f5 grant (refuses with a named error pointing at `flow epic grant`). On every observed merge the loop calls `flow-exec-review review --kind wave --epic <slug>` once (serially, never mid-launch), and applies only a reorder (launch order of unstarted features within the frontier). A proposal (defer, cut, add a feature, change the goal) is never applied: it shows as one board line + `flow-notify` with the rationale, and the affected feature waits until the owner answers; an owner `yes` goes through the `/flow-epic-run` amend-manifest route — the loop never edits the manifest. `escalate` ⇒ hold that branch with one owner-needed line. The board gains a digest line ('N decisions made for you since you last looked — log at …') and per-feature lines show `approved by executive (decision <id>)`. Executive failure or skip ⇒ the loop keeps launching per f1 rules and shows `executive unavailable — launching per manifest order`. Model/effort: the manager's `--model/--effort` override the grant's for executive calls. Tests next door: merge ⇒ one review, reorder applied only to unstarted nodes, proposal ⇒ hold + notify and no manifest change, escalate ⇒ hold + notify, no grant ⇒ zero model calls, executive failure ⇒ f1 behaviour.

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `f3-sequencer-executive`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides how the zero-token loop hands decision points to the executive without becoming judgment itself (the PR #420 lesson): the loop only triggers and displays; f5 decides.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN the sequencer observes a merged feature and an owner grant is live THE SYSTEM SHALL run exactly one f5 wave review before its next launch, apply a reorder only to unstarted features, and log it

WHEN a wave review returns escalate, or proposes deferring, cutting or adding a feature or changing the epic goal THE SYSTEM SHALL launch nothing further on the affected branch and show one owner-needed board line with the proposal and its rationale

WHEN decisions were made under the grant THE SYSTEM SHALL show a board digest line counting them by kind with the log path, and each status refresh SHALL name any decision made since the owner last looked
WHEN no grant is live THE SYSTEM SHALL behave exactly as f1 (observe) and make zero model calls
WHEN the sequencer was started with --model and --effort THE SYSTEM SHALL pass them to the executive review in place of the grant's defaults

features.title: Wait node: the `## UI review` section has shipped
features.description:
Wait node — do not build anything. This node is satisfied when the PR from the separate flow pipeline `add-ui-ux-critique-improve` has merged; that pipeline adds the machine-written `## UI review` section (a critic's remaining findings, every `SUBJECTIVE:` line left unticked) that `f4-delegated-ui-signoff` reads as evidence. On 2026-10-25 it was at `plan-pending-review` with no PR. The owner records it with `flow epic bind re-design-epic-manager-agent w2-ui-review-section --external "<that PR>"`. If a pipeline was launched from this node by mistake, make no code change, stop at triage as no-change, and report that this node must be bound with `flow epic bind ... --external` instead.

Part of epic `re-design-epic-manager-agent` (feature `w2-ui-review-section`) — design at `.flow/epics/re-design-epic-manager-agent/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D7 (second condition): delegated UI sign-off reads a section another pipeline is still building; the frontier waits for it.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN the owner binds this node with flow epic bind --external THE SYSTEM SHALL classify it merged and unblock f4-delegated-ui-signoff
WHEN this node is unbound THE SYSTEM SHALL never launch it (flow epic launch refuses a waitFor node)
features.waitFor: the PR from pipeline add-ui-ux-critique-improve merged (adds the ## UI review section)

features.title: Evidence-first `SUBJECTIVE:` sign-off: one-action by default, delegated on a second opt-in
features.description:
Make `SUBJECTIVE:` UI sign-off evidence-first, and let a managed epic's pipeline tick those items itself only under a second explicit owner opt-in with a non-Claude reviewer agreeing. Default (no extra grant, every pipeline): when step 9's `flow-gate-decide` returns `gated` with `SUBJECTIVE:` items open, the GATED block (`flow-gate-summary`) carries, per item, the screenshots for every viewport and theme it names and the `## UI review` summary, so the owner judges and ticks in one action without hunting. Delegated (class `subjective`, granted only by `flow epic grant <epic> --autonomy high --delegate-ui`, recorded in f5's `grant.json`): before rendering GATED, an epic feature runs `flow-exec-review review --kind ui` (f5's executive review with the charter's end-user-expectation lens), which approves only when the PR body's `## UI review` section exists with no remaining `major` or `defect` finding, screenshots exist for every viewport and theme each open item names, a non-Claude reviewer via `flow-delegate` independently views the screenshots and agrees with the in-pipeline UI critique (fail closed when `flow-delegate` is unavailable or cannot read the images), and no `DECISION:` or `Browser:` item and no other gate reason is open. Pass ⇒ tick only those `SUBJECTIVE:` items, post one evidence comment on the PR (screenshots, critique summary, reviewer verdict, decision id), record the decision in the epic log, then take a NEW non-override branch in `skills/pipeline/flow-pipeline/references/phases/step-09-gate.md`: re-run `flow-gate-decide "$PR"`; `auto-merge` (all items ticked, `autoMerge` not false) ⇒ step 10, with the log entry stating the merge came from a gate re-check under `autoMerge`, not from any instruction; anything else ⇒ route per the normal table. It never calls `flow-merge-guard --record-override`, never fires the gate-override form, and with `autoMerge: false` still stops at `gated` for the owner's 'merge'. features.rationale: Hides D6: the UI evidence bar, the non-Claude agreement check, and the non-override gate re-check that is the only path from a delegated tick to a merge.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a PR is gated with SUBJECTIVE items open and no subjective grant THE SYSTEM SHALL render the screenshots per named viewport and theme and the UI review summary in the GATED block

WHEN the subjective class is granted and the evidence bar holds and the non-Claude reviewer agrees THE SYSTEM SHALL tick only the SUBJECTIVE items, post one evidence comment, record the decision, and re-run flow-gate-decide
WHEN the re-check returns auto-merge THE SYSTEM SHALL proceed to step 10 and log that the merge came from a gate re-check under autoMerge, and WHEN autoMerge is false it SHALL stay gated
WHEN a DECISION or Browser item is open, the UI review has a major or defect finding, a named screenshot is missing, or flow-delegate cannot read the images THE SYSTEM SHALL not tick anything
THE SYSTEM SHALL never call flow-merge-guard --record-override or fire the gate-override form on this path (lint anchor in bin/skill-md-lint.test.ts)
WHEN a Claude-side model call is made for a delegated UI sign-off THE SYSTEM SHALL use the model and effort recorded in the sequencer's manager.json
